docs.title: RiffPi
docs.text:
This site documents RiffPi, the control daemon for Kleag's MFX, a guitar multi-effect pedalboard built around a Raspberry Pi, a Pisound sound card, and Guitarix as the effects engine, housed in a repurposed wooden box. Foot switches, rotary encoders, a keypad, a joystick, and an expression pedal all drive Guitarix over MIDI.

I'm currently at hardware version 2.2.1 of the pedal.

docs.text:

  • Usage — what each control does and how it maps to MIDI.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
RiffPi is a small Python daemon that reads a set of physical controls on the pedalboard and turns them into MIDI Control Change (CC) and Program Change messages sent to Guitarix over a virtual MIDI port.

It's installed as the riffpi command (CLI dispatch in riffpi.cli:main). Running riffpi (or riffpi run) starts the daemon itself (riffpi.daemon:run); riffpi install-service / riffpi uninstall-service manage the systemd --user service — see Installation.

docs.title: Hardware overview
docs.text:
Everything is wired to the Raspberry Pi over a single I2C bus:

  • Two MCP23017 16-bit GPIO expanders (0x20 and 0x21) provide the digital I/O for the 4 foot switches + LEDs, the 4 rotary encoders (with their push buttons), the 4x4 matrix keypad, and the joystick's push button.
  • One ADS1115 4-channel ADC reads the two analog joystick axes and the expression pedal.
  • A Pisound sound card provides the audio interface and, via PipeWire, the MIDI bridge to Guitarix running on the same Raspberry Pi 5.
graph LR
    subgraph Pi["Raspberry Pi 5"]
        I2C["I2C bus"]
        MCP1["MCP23017 @0x20<br/>foot switches, encoders A"]
        MCP2["MCP23017 @0x21<br/>keypad, encoders B"]
        ADS["ADS1115<br/>joystick X/Y, expr. pedal"]
        RiffPi["riffpi daemon"]
        Guitarix["Guitarix<br/>(gx_head_amp)"]
        Pisound["Pisound"]
    end
    I2C --- MCP1
    I2C --- MCP2
    I2C --- ADS
    MCP1 --> RiffPi
    MCP2 --> RiffPi
    ADS --> RiffPi
    RiffPi -- "MIDI CC (virtual port 'KleagMFX')" --> Guitarix
    Guitarix -- "MIDI CC echo" --> RiffPi
    Guitarix --- Pisound

docs.title: Software architecture
docs.text:
riffpi.daemon.run() does all hardware/MIDI setup, then starts one daemon thread per input device plus a MIDI-input listener thread, and blocks on signal.pause():

  • pipewire_link_thread — every 2 seconds, checks (pw-link -l) that the virtual MIDI port is linked both ways to Guitarix's gx_head_amp ports and creates any missing link (pw-link), so Guitarix can start after RiffPi or be restarted without restarting RiffPi.
  • midi_input_thread — listens on the same virtual MIDI port for CC echoes coming back from Guitarix (e.g. after a preset change alters effect state) and re-syncs local LED/encoder state.
  • buttons_thread — polls the 4 foot switches (debounced via MCPButton).
  • joystick.poll_joystick — reads the ADS1115, emits relative mouse motion via uinput.
  • keypad.keypad_thread — scans the 4x4 matrix keypad.
  • expression_pedal.poll — reads the ADS1115, sends smoothed CC24 values.
  • one rotary_encoder.poll_thread per encoder — quadrature decoding + CC deltas.
  • main_thread_loop — drains task_queue (currently only the "reset" action queued by the keypad when switching preset banks).

Foot switch buttons and every encoder's built-in push button route through the same handle_effect_toggle(idx) callback. The last encoder is special-cased there as the preset-bank selector (cycles Guitarix banks A-D) instead of toggling an effect; turning that same encoder (handled separately, in RotaryEncoder.handle_rotation) instead changes preset within the current bank, wrapping at however many presets that bank actually has — looked up live via riffpi.guitarix_rpc.GuitarixRPC (Guitarix's JSON-RPC control port, guitarix -p PORT), falling back to an un-wrapped 0-127 clamp if that port isn't reachable.

i2c_lock (a threading.Lock) guards ADS1115 reads shared between the Joystick and ExpressionPedal threads, since both poll the same ADS1115 instance concurrently.

docs.title: Driver modules
docs.text:
Module Responsibility riffpi.rotary_encoder Quadrature decoding (transition lookup table) → relative MIDI CC deltas riffpi.guitarix_rpc Read-only JSON-RPC client (raw TCP, no HTTP) for Guitarix's -p PORT control port; used to size the preset-encoder wraparound riffpi.keypad 4x4 matrix scan; digit-buffer preset entry; */# as mouse left/right click riffpi.joystick ADS1115 → dead-zone/power-curve shaped relative mouse motion (see Usage) riffpi.expression_pedal ADS1115 → median-smoothed MIDI CC24 riffpi.mcp_button / riffpi.mcp_led Thin per-pin MCP23017 button/LED wrappers

See Usage for the full MIDI CC mapping and what each control does.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: This covers setting up a Raspberry Pi to run RiffPi end to end: enabling I2C, installing the package, configuring virtual mouse input permissions, and running it as a background service.

docs.title: Hardware / OS prerequisites
docs.text:
• Raspberry Pi 5 (a Pi 4 should also work).
  • Pisound sound card.
  • The MCP23017 (×2) and ADS1115 I2C peripherals wired up as described in Architecture.

docs.title: Enable I2C and the Pisound overlay
docs.text:
Add to /boot/firmware/config.txt:

display_auto_detect=1
dtparam=i2c_arm=on
dtparam=spi=on
dtparam=i2c_arm_baudrate=400000
dtoverlay=pisound
dtoverlay=vc4-kms-v3d
usb_max_current_enable=1

Then enable I2C interactively and reboot:

sudo raspi-config

Go to Interface Options → I2C → Enable, then reboot.

docs.title: Verify the I2C devices are visible
docs.text:
sudo apt install -y i2c-tools
sudo i2cdetect -y 1

You should see the two MCP23017s (0x20, 0x21) and the ADS1115 on the bus.

docs.title: Set up the virtual mouse device (uinput)
docs.text:
The joystick and keypad emulate mouse input via uinput, which needs the kernel module loaded and the running user to have permission to open it:

sudo apt install python3-uinput
echo uinput | sudo tee -a /etc/modules

sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-uinput.rules <<'EOF'
KERNEL=="uinput", SUBSYSTEM=="misc", MODE="0660", GROUP="input"
EOF
sudo usermod -a -G input $USER

Log out and back in (or reboot) for the group change to take effect.

docs.title: Install and autostart Guitarix and guitariqx
docs.text:
RiffPi is only the controller: the sound itself is processed by Guitarix, running on the same Pi under PipeWire's JACK emulation. Guitarix runs headless, as a server (-N, no GUI of its own), and the touchscreen shows guitariqx, a Qt 6 touch-friendly GUI that drives it over its JSON-RPC port.

Until the pull requests made to upstream Guitarix for this setup are merged, use the kleag fork of Guitarix, installed from its apt repository, rather than the distribution's guitarix package. Its guitarix-kleag package replaces (and conflicts with) the distribution's guitarix* packages and installs the same /usr/bin/guitarix binary. Packages are built for Debian Bookworm (Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm) and Ubuntu Resolute only, not yet for Trixie:

sudo install -d /etc/apt/keyrings
sudo curl -fsSLo /etc/apt/keyrings/kleag-guitarix.asc https://kleag.github.io/guitarix/kleag-guitarix.asc
sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kleag-guitarix.sources <<EOF
Types: deb
URIs: https://kleag.github.io/guitarix
Suites: $(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME")
Components: main
Signed-By: /etc/apt/keyrings/kleag-guitarix.asc
EOF
sudo apt update
sudo apt install guitarix-kleag pipewire-jack

If the distribution's guitarix was already installed, apt replaces it. Once the changes are merged upstream, going back to the distribution package is a matter of removing the .sources file and running sudo apt install guitarix.

Install guitariqx from its own apt repository, so it is upgraded with the rest of the system by apt upgrade. apt pulls in the Qt modules it needs. Packages are built for Debian Bookworm (Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm), Trixie and Ubuntu Resolute. Its key is saved under its own name, so that it doesn't overwrite the Guitarix repository's kleag-guitarix.asc, which holds an extra key:

sudo install -d /etc/apt/keyrings
sudo curl -fsSLo /etc/apt/keyrings/kleag-guitariqx.asc https://kleag.github.io/guitariqx/apt/kleag-guitarix.asc
sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/guitariqx.sources <<EOF
Types: deb
URIs: https://kleag.github.io/guitariqx/apt
Suites: $(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME")
Components: main
Signed-By: /etc/apt/keyrings/kleag-guitariqx.asc
EOF
sudo apt update
sudo apt install guitariqx

If guitariqx was previously installed from a downloaded .deb, this repository takes over its upgrades; nothing needs to be removed first.

docs.title: Guitarix server (systemd user service)
docs.text:
Without its GUI, Guitarix no longer needs the display, so it runs as a systemd --user service, like RiffPi itself, which restarts it if it crashes. Create ~/.config/systemd/user/guitarix.service:

[Unit]
Description=Guitarix engine (headless server)
After=pipewire.service wireplumber.service
Wants=pipewire.service wireplumber.service

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/bin/pw-jack /usr/bin/guitarix -N -p 7777
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target

then enable and start it:

systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now guitarix.service
  • pw-jack runs Guitarix against PipeWire's JACK implementation.
  • -N starts Guitarix without its own GUI (server mode).
  • -p 7777 opens Guitarix's JSON-RPC control port, used both by guitariqx and by RiffPi (to know how many presets each bank holds, see Usage). It must match GUITARIX_RPC_PORT at the top of riffpi/daemon.py.

Check it with systemctl --user status guitarix.service and journalctl --user-unit guitarix.service -f. To start on boot with nobody logged in, enable lingering (see below).

docs.title: guitariqx in fullscreen (desktop autostart)
docs.text:
guitariqx is a GUI application, so start it from the desktop session's autostart rather than as a systemd service (it needs the Wayland display, which systemd user services don't get by default). Create ~/.config/autostart/guitariqx.desktop:

[Desktop Entry]
Type=Application
Name=guitariqx
Exec=guitariqx -f -p 7777
  • -f runs guitariqx fullscreen, for the touchscreen.
  • -p 7777 connects it to the Guitarix server's JSON-RPC port (guitariqx defaults to 7000, so it must be given explicitly). Guitarix runs on the same Pi, so the default host, localhost, is right.

Startup order doesn't matter: guitariqx reconnects by itself when the Guitarix server starts or restarts. The desktop session starts it at login, so on a headless pedal enable automatic desktop login (sudo raspi-config → System Options → Boot / Auto Login → Desktop Autologin). Nothing restarts guitariqx if it is closed: relaunch it from a terminal or log out and back in.

Startup order between Guitarix and RiffPi doesn't matter either: RiffPi checks every 2 seconds that its MIDI port is linked to Guitarix's (gx_head_amp) through PipeWire, and creates the links as soon as Guitarix's ports appear, including after Guitarix is restarted. Until then its log shows "Guitarix MIDI ports not available".

If you previously autostarted Guitarix with its own GUI, remove ~/.config/autostart/guitarix.desktop, otherwise a second Guitarix instance fights the server for the port and the Pisound.

docs.title: Install RiffPi
docs.text:
pip install riffpi

This installs the riffpi command. Running riffpi with no arguments (or riffpi run) runs the daemon directly in the foreground — useful to check everything works before setting it up as a background service.

docs.title: Run as a systemd user service
docs.text:
pip install never installs or enables background services on its own — that's a deliberate, separate step. riffpi ships a subcommand for it:

riffpi install-service

This writes ~/.config/systemd/user/riffpi.service (pointing ExecStart at wherever riffpi was actually installed), then runs the equivalent of:

systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now riffpi.service

so the daemon starts immediately and again on every future login. Useful follow-up commands:

systemctl --user status riffpi.service
journalctl --user-unit riffpi.service -f
systemctl --user stop riffpi.service

To remove it again:

riffpi uninstall-service

which stops, disables, and deletes the unit file.

docs.title: Starting on boot without logging in (headless)
docs.text:
A systemd --user service normally only runs while its user has an active login session. For a pedal that should come up on boot with nobody logged in, enable "lingering" for your user once:

sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER

riffpi install-service checks this and prints a reminder if it isn't enabled yet.

docs.title: Doing it manually
docs.text:
If you'd rather not run the installer, or need a non-standard setup, here's the unit file it writes, for reference:

[Unit]
Description=RiffPi Guitar Multi-Effect Daemon
After=graphical-session.target

[Service]
ExecStart=/home/<you>/.venv/bin/riffpi
WorkingDirectory=/home/<you>
Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target

Save it as ~/.config/systemd/user/riffpi.service (adjusting ExecStart to wherever riffpi was installed, e.g. which riffpi), then run the systemctl --user commands above yourself.

docs.title: Screen rotation (keypad 999)
docs.text:
Typing 999 on the keypad toggles the screen between portrait and landscape (handled by riffpi/display.py, which calls wlr-randr; Wayland desktop only, the Raspberry Pi OS default).

  1. Install the tool: sudo apt install wlr-randr. Run wlr-randr to see your output's name (e.g. DSI-1).

  2. Make touches follow the rotation by mapping the touchscreen to that output in ~/.config/labwc/rc.xml (get the device name from libinput list-devices), then log out and back in:

    <touch deviceName="your touchscreen name" mapToOutput="DSI-1" />

  3. If the screen comes out upside down after a toggle, set QUARTER_TURN_TRANSFORM = "270" at the top of riffpi/display.py. If several outputs are connected, set DISPLAY_OUTPUT.

The rotation is not saved: after a reboot the screen is back in its configured orientation.

docs.title: Mixer mode (keypad 998)
docs.text:
Typing 998 turns the pedal's screen into the remote control of a digital mixer with a web GUI, set up for a Soundcraft Ui24R (handled by riffpi/mixer.py):

  • on: joins the mixer's Wi-Fi (nmcli), rotates to landscape, opens the GUI in Chromium kiosk mode;
  • off: closes Chromium, rotates back to portrait, reconnects the previously active Wi-Fi.

Setup:

  1. Do the screen rotation setup above.
  2. Set MIXER_WIFI_SSID at the top of riffpi/mixer.py to the mixer's network name (the network is assumed to have no password). MIXER_URL defaults to http://10.10.1.1, the Ui24R's address on its own hotspot.
  3. Check Chromium is installed (sudo apt install chromium if chromium isn't found).
  4. Check the riffpi service is allowed to switch networks: from the pedal, type 998 and watch journalctl --user-unit riffpi.service -f. A "Not authorized" error from nmcli means NetworkManager's polkit rules don't let this user change connections outside a desktop session; a polkit rule granting org.freedesktop.NetworkManager.* to this user is then needed.

The first time, the Pi creates a saved connection for the mixer's network; it then joins it in a few seconds. While in mixer mode the Pi is off your usual Wi-Fi. If the mixer is cabled to the Pi's Ethernet port instead, set MIXER_URL to http://10.10.2.1 (the Ui24R's wired default); a failed Wi-Fi join is logged but the GUI is still opened.

docs.title: Disable WiFi power management
docs.text:
To avoid losing WiFi unexpectedly on the Pi, disable its power management. Create /etc/systemd/system/wifi-fix.service:

[Unit]
Description=Disable WiFi Power Management
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/sbin/iwconfig wlan0 power off
RemainAfterExit=yes

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

sudo systemctl enable wifi-fix.service
sudo systemctl start wifi-fix.service

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: Once riffpi is running (see Installation) and linked to Guitarix over PipeWire MIDI, the pedalboard's controls behave as follows.

docs.title: Foot switches
docs.text:
4 foot switches with LEDs toggle Guitarix effects on/off. Pressing a switch flips its state, lights/dims its LED, and sends a MIDI CC. If Guitarix reports a state change back (e.g. after loading a preset), the LED updates to match automatically.

Foot switch MIDI CC 1 64 2 65 3 66 4 67

docs.title: Rotary encoders
docs.text:
The first 3 rotary encoders send relative MIDI CC changes as they're turned — each detent moves its CC value by ±5 (clamped to 0-127). This is meant for continuous Guitarix parameters (gain, tone, etc.) rather than on/off effects.

Encoder MIDI CC 1 20 2 21 3 22

The 4th (preset) encoder works differently: turning it moves to the next/previous preset within the current bank (a Program Change, one per detent), wrapping around at however many presets are actually defined in that bank rather than clamping at 127. This wraparound is looked up live over Guitarix's JSON-RPC control port — start Guitarix with guitarix -N -p 7777 (see Install and autostart Guitarix and guitariqx, and GUITARIX_RPC_HOST/GUITARIX_RPC_PORT in riffpi/daemon.py to use a different port) for this to work; if that port isn't reachable, preset changes still work but fall back to an un-wrapped 0-127 clamp. Its push button instead cycles through Guitarix preset banks A → B → C → D → A... (sends CC0=2, then CC32 = bank index, then a Program Change selecting the bank's first preset — Guitarix ignores CC32 unless CC0=2 precedes it). The other three encoders' buttons behave like extra foot switches.

docs.title: Keypad
docs.text:
A 4x4 matrix keypad selects presets directly and doubles as mouse buttons:

  • A / B / C / D — select preset bank A-D immediately (same effect as cycling with the last encoder's button, but direct).
  • 0-9 — type a preset number. Digits typed within 0.4s of each other accumulate (e.g. 1 then 2 within the window selects preset 12); after 0.4s of no further digits, the number is sent as a Program Change and the buffer resets.
  • 9 9 9 — instead of selecting a preset, toggles the screen between portrait and landscape (e.g. to use the pedal's screen for a mixer's web GUI). See Screen rotation for the one-time setup.
  • 9 9 8 — enters or leaves mixer mode: the Pi joins the mixer's Wi-Fi, turns the screen to landscape and opens the mixer's web GUI full screen; typing it again closes it, goes back to portrait and to the previous Wi-Fi. See Mixer mode.
  • * — virtual mouse left click (held down while the key is held).
  • # — virtual mouse right click (held down while the key is held).

Selecting a bank or preset resets all foot-switch effect states/LEDs, since Guitarix presets define their own effect chain.

docs.title: Joystick
docs.text:
The analog joystick moves the mouse pointer — useful for dragging Guitarix's on-screen knobs to fine-tune a parameter without leaving the pedalboard. Pushing the joystick in also acts as a middle-click.

Cursor speed ramps up smoothly from the center: small deflections move the pointer slowly (for precise knob nudges), and only a large deflection reaches full speed. Raw readings are smoothed to filter out electrical noise from the joystick's potentiometers, and the center position is measured automatically each time riffpi starts (so it doesn't need to be physically centered with high precision). If the feel still isn't right for your hardware, SENSITIVITY, DEAD_ZONE, POWER_CURVE, and SMOOTHING_WINDOW at the top of riffpi/joystick.py are the constants to tune — see the comments there for what each one does.

docs.title: Expression pedal
docs.text: The expression pedal sends MIDI CC 24, mapped from its measured voltage range and smoothed with a rolling median filter to avoid jitter.

docs.title: MIDI CC reference
docs.text: Control MIDI CC(s) Foot switches 1-4 64-67 Rotary encoders 1-3 20-22 Preset encoder: preset change (turn) Program Change Preset encoder: bank change (click) 0=2 (bank-select mode), 32 (bank), Program Change (first preset in bank) Expression pedal 24
